arxiv-2103-02478.title: On lower estimations of square-linear ratio for plane Peano curves.
arxiv-2103-02478.creator: E. V. Shchepin , E. Yu. Mychka
arxiv-2103-02478.description: Abstract It is proved that for any mapping of a unit segment to a unit square, there is a pair of points of the segment for which the square of the Euclidean distance between their images exceeds the distance between them on the segment by at least 3 ⁤ 5 8 3\frac{5}{8} times.

arxiv-2210-00787.title: Demystification of Entangled Mass Action Law
arxiv-2210-00787.creator: A. N. Kirdin, S. V. Stasenko
arxiv-2210-00787.description: Abstract Recently, Gorban (2021) analysed some kinetic paradoxes of the transition state theory and proposed its revision that gave the “entangled mass action law”, in which new reactions were generated as an addition to the reaction mechanism under consideration. These paradoxes arose due to the assumption of quasiequilibrium between reactants and transition states.

arxiv-2301-09246.title: On the Biplanarity of Blowups
arxiv-2301-09246.creator: David Eppstein
arxiv-2301-09246.description: Abstract The 2-blowup of a graph is obtained by replacing each vertex with two non-adjacent copies; a graph is biplanar if it is the union of two planar graphs. We disprove a conjecture of Gethner that 2-blowups of planar graphs are biplanar: iterated Kleetopes are counterexamples.

arxiv-2307-14840.title: State preparation by shallow circuits using feed forward
arxiv-2307-14840.creator: Harry Buhrman, Marten Folkertsma, Bruno Loff, Niels M. P. Neumann
arxiv-2307-14840.description: Abstract Fault tolerant quantum computers repetitively apply a four-step procedure: First, perform a few one and two-qubit quantum gates. Second, perform a syndrome measurement on a subset of the qubits. Third, perform fast classical computations to establish if and where errors occurred. And, fourth, correct the errors with a correction step.

arxiv-2312-06867.title: Get an A in Math: Progressive Rectification Prompting
arxiv-2312-06867.creator: Zhenyu Wu, Meng Jiang, Chao Shen
arxiv-2312-06867.description: Abstract Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting methods have enabled large language models (LLMs) to generate reasoning paths and solve math word problems (MWPs). However, they are sensitive to mistakes in the paths, as any mistake can result in an incorrect answer. We propose a novel method named Progressive Rectification Prompting (PRP) to improve average accuracy on eight MWP datasets from 77.3 77.

arxiv-2412-16199.title: Stabilizing Machine Learning for Reproducible and Explainable Results: A Novel Validation Approach to Subject-Specific Insights
arxiv-2412-16199.creator: Gideon Vos, Liza van Eijk, Zoltan Sarnyai, Mostafa Rahimi Azghadi
arxiv-2412-16199.description: Abstract Introduction Machine Learning (ML) is transforming medical research by enhancing diagnostic accuracy, predicting disease progression, and personalizing treatments. While general models trained on large datasets identify broad patterns across populations, the diversity of human biology, shaped by genetics, environment, and lifestyle, often limits their effectiveness.

arxiv-2505-11609.title: Ultraviolet variability in Solar-type members of the M67 open cluster Facilities: GALEX
arxiv-2505-11609.creator: Carl Melis, Ekamjot Kaire
arxiv-2505-11609.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Carl Melis, Ekamjot Kaire. Solar-type members of the rich, nearly Solar-age and Solar-metallicity M67 open cluster are systematically investigated for ultraviolet variability. We utilize archival Galaxy Evolution Explorer ( GALEX ) data which features several imaging observation epochs spanning 5 years. Stars in or suspected of being in binary systems are avoided as well as stars that are blended in GALEX data, leading to a sample of 66 Solar-type stars.

arxiv-2509-07589.title: Unusual magnetic order in Eu 10 Hg 55
arxiv-2509-07589.creator: Rachel Nixon, Nazar Zaremba, Samuel A. Adegboyega, Andreas Leithe-Jasper, Mitja Krnel, Yurii Prots, Ulrich Burkhardt, Jörg Sichelschmidt, Lucia Amidani, Fabio La Mattina, Michael Shatruk, Alexander Shengelaya, Manuel Brando, Eteri Svanidze
arxiv-2509-07589.description: Abstract In solid-state compounds, the valence of europium can sometimes be mixed – which is especially favored in structures with several positions for the europium atoms. In this work, we study the Eu-based intermetallic noncentrosymmetric system Eu 10 Hg 55 which has 65 atoms per unit cell and 4 distinct crystallographic positions for europium and 17 positions for mercury.

arxiv-2601-08778.title: Pervasive Annotation Errors Break Text-to-SQL Benchmarks and Leaderboards
arxiv-2601-08778.creator: Tengjun Jin, Yoojin Choi, Yuxuan Zhu, Daniel Kang
arxiv-2601-08778.description: Abstract . Researchers have proposed numerous text-to-SQL techniques to streamline data analytics and accelerate the development of data-driven applications. To compare these techniques and select the best one for deployment, the community depends on public benchmarks and their leaderboards. Since these benchmarks heavily rely on human annotations during question construction and answer evaluation, the validity of the annotations is crucial.

pmc-10663967.title: Physicians’ Perceptions of Clinical Decision Support to Treat Patients With Heart Failure in the ED
pmc-10663967.creator: Scott D. Casey, Mary E. Reed, Chris LeMaster, Dustin G. Mark, Jesse Gaskin, Robert P. Norris, Dana R. Sax
pmc-10663967.description: Key PointsQuestionWhat are physicians’ perceptions of using a novel clinical decision support intervention that displays risk estimates, collates relevant clinical information, and provides treatment recommendations for patients with acute heart failure in the emergency department?FindingsIn this qualitative study with 58 emergency department physicians, participants identified several actionable items that they believed would enhance clinical decision support usability and workflow integration.

pmc-11367864.title: Reliability of pre-resection ligament tension assessment in imageless robotic assisted total knee replacement
pmc-11367864.creator: Dennis K. H. Yee, Jonathan T. C. Leung, Vikki Chu, Gene Man, Gloria Y. T. Lam, Jimmy K. Y. Lau, Tsz-Lung Choi, Wai-Wang Chau, Jonathan Patrick Ng, Michael Tim-Yun Ong, Kevin Ki-Wai Ho, Patrick Shu-Hang Yung
pmc-11367864.description: BackgroundLigament tension balance is a major determinant for the success of total knee replacement (TKR). The present study aimed at determining the inter-rater and intra-rater reliability in performing ligament tension assessment using an imageless robotic-assisted TKR.MethodsTwenty-four knees in 21 patients who received robotic-assisted TKR for end-stage varus osteoarthritis were examined.

pmc-12395831.title: To tier or not to tier: the institutionalization of the World Health Organization’s power to determine pandemic emergency in the amended International Health Regulations (2005)
pmc-12395831.creator: Yi Zhang, Yida Guo
pmc-12395831.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The binary nature of a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) alert was brought to attention during COVID-19, with the COVID-19 IHR Emergency Committee and some States Parties advocating for an intermediate or regional tier of warning. However, the recent amendments to the International Health Regulations (2005) yielded an unexpected outcome: no proposed lower tier was added to the binary alert framework; instead, ‘pandemic emergency’ was introduced as a tier of alert within the PHEIC framework.

pmc-12609868.title: Cranial Morphological Patterns Based on Cranial Index and Petrous Ridge–Midline Angle in Koreans: Implications for Clinical and Forensic Applications

pmc-12609868.description: Background: The human skull has a very complex and diverse structure, and morphological characteristics vary by population. The purpose of this study is to comprehensively analyze the cranial morphology using postmortem computed tomography (PMCT), and to identify anatomical characteristics through a multifaceted approach in Koreans.

pmc-12732238.title: B Cells Can Trigger the T-Cell-Mediated Autoimmune Response Against Melanocytes in Psoriasis
pmc-12732238.creator: Mengwen He, Melissa Bernhardt, Akiko Arakawa, Song-Min Kim, Sigrid Vollmer, Burkard Summer, Yukiyasu Arakawa, Tatsushi Ishimoto, Andreas Schlosser, Jörg Christoph Prinz, Christian Sadik
pmc-12732238.description: Highlights What are the main findings? We find that under inflammatory conditions, B cells from streptococci-infected tonsils and blood of HLA-C*06:02-positive psoriasis patients activate a melanocyte-reactive T-cell receptor from a pathogenic psoriatic CD8+ T cell clone and also have autostimulatory properties for CD8+ T cells.

pmc-12994166.title: Psoriasis-like disease prevents squamous skin tumor development by neutrophil-driven inflammation
pmc-12994166.creator: Panagiota Tsokkou, Martin Holcmann, Katharina Rindler, Kamil Mieczkowski, Lisa Shaw, Matthias Farlik, Maria Sibilia, Erwin F. Wagner
pmc-12994166.description: SignificanceThis study challenges the prevailing view that chronic inflammation is uniformly tumor-promoting. By demonstrating that psoriasis-like inflammation prevents cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma development in different mouse models, it provides mechanistic insights into how sustained immune activation can instead limit cancer susceptibility.

pmc-13267771.title: Myeloperoxidase impairs mucociliary transport on human airway epithelium
pmc-13267771.creator: Allison Boboltz, Vaidehi Rathi, Sahana Kumar, Gregg A Duncan
pmc-13267771.description: Dampening neutrophil-driven inflammation in the airways remains a challenge in treating cystic fibrosis (CF) lung disease. Myeloperoxidase (MPO) is a neutrophilic enzyme that produces reactive oxygen species and is highly concentrated in CF airways. Greater MPO concentrations have previously been correlated with increased mucus plugging in bronchiectasis, suggesting that MPO could impair mucociliary transport.

pmc-13350226.title: Impaired hematopoiesis affects apheresis and CAR T‐cell product composition and treatment response
pmc-13350226.creator: Hanna Kuhn, Felix Korell, Angela Hückelhoven‐Krauss, Brigitte Neuber, Miriam Stenzinger, Anita Ludwig‐Husemann, Maria‐Luisa Schubert, Patrick Derigs, Kiavasch Farid, Tim Sauer, Sandra Sauer, Carsten Müller‐Tidow, Peter Dreger, Michael Schmitt, Anita Schmitt
pmc-13350226.description: BackgroundChimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T‐cell therapy has transformed the treatment of hematologic malignancies, but its success depends on obtaining sufficient CD3+ T‐cell yields during leukapheresis. This can be difficult in heavily pretreated patients, who often show leukopenia and reduced T‐cell fitness.
